title: Paws by the Pond
checkpoint: Phase 5 (School readiness) — new sound 'aw' (the /or/ sound as in paw, saw and crawl)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 5 book for the new sound 'aw' — another way to write the /or/ sound your child knows from 'fork', used in paw, saw, crawl and yawn. Every other word uses sounds from Phases 2 to 4.

pages.text: Ned saw a big paw print.
pages.illustration: Ned staring down at a single large paw print in the mud, drawn crisp and clear and considerably bigger than his own foot. Ominous and exciting.
The print in close-up: four toe pads and a heel pressed into wet brown mud, water gathering in it. Detailed and slightly menacing.

pages.text: Was it a fox? said Ned.
pages.illustration: Ned looking around the reeds with wide eyes, imagining — show a faint fox shape suggested in the shadows behind the stems.
Ned crawling forward on his belly through the grass in full stealth mode, only his eyes above the stems. Very funny.

pages.text: He saw a claw in the grass.
pages.illustration: A single curved claw caught on a grass stem, gleaming, drawn large. Ned's beak inches from it.

pages.text: It was just a big cat!
pages.illustration: Reveal: a big fat tabby cat lying in the sun beside the pond, entirely harmless and half asleep. Ned's whole body slumping with relief.

pages.text: The cat let out a yawn.
pages.illustration: The cat mid-yawn, enormous pink mouth and curled tongue, teeth on full display but comic rather than scary.
Ned yawning back at the cat, beak wide, in unconscious imitation. The two of them mirroring each other. Charming.

pages.text: It was dawn. Ned went to bed.
pages.illustration: Closing page: pale dawn light over the pond, the cat asleep, Ned waddling off to bed with his eyes already closing.
